The 28-year-old suspect, identified as Greene Da’monte Khiree, was arrested shortly after arriving in Nigeria aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand through Dubai.
According to the NDLEA, the suspect attempted to evade security checks after abandoning two checked-in bags and proceeding towards the airport exit with only his hand luggage.
However, operatives monitoring his movements intercepted him at the airport car park.
A search of the abandoned luggage, which bore his name tags, led to the discovery of 32 parcels of Loud weighing 33.95kg, alongside a tracking device.
During interrogation, the suspect, a native of Savannah, Georgia, reportedly told investigators that he had been living in Thailand since October 2025, where he played professional basketball.
He also claimed that he travelled to Nigeria on holiday to establish networks that could advance his basketball career.
NDLEA’s spokesperson, Femi Babafemi, said the arrest formed part of a series of nationwide operations by the anti-narcotics agency, which also resulted in the interception of 25.05kg of methamphetamine concealed in breakfast cereal packs at the same airport.
The agency said the methamphetamine consignment was intercepted on November 11 at the arrival hall of Terminal II following the arrest of a 56-year-old suspect, Omokan Isaac Babatope, whose real name was given as Chinedu Onwude.
A search of his two travelling boxes led to the discovery of 25 parcels of methamphetamine concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products.
The suspect, who reportedly lived in South Africa for over 24 years, allegedly confessed to using a false identity obtained through forged documents to facilitate his entry into Nigeria.
He reportedly told investigators that a South Africa-based individual, identified as Obiora Okoye, contracted him to deliver the drugs in Nigeria for R20,000.
In another operation, NDLEA operatives dismantled an illegal firearms manufacturing factory at Sabon Garin Kangin, Kaduna State, arresting a 45-year-old suspect, Sagiru Musa.
The November 9 operation led to the recovery of 17 locally made Dane guns, two pistols, 25 Dane gun pipes and other materials allegedly used in the manufacture of firearms.
Similarly, operatives intercepted a 31-year-old woman, Tabara Dauda, along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway with 196 rounds of live AK-47 ammunition and N675,000 cash.
The agency also reported the seizure of large quantities of illicit drugs in separate operations across Lagos, Kaduna, Ondo, Delta, Edo and Osun states.
The NDLEA said the operations underscored its commitment to disrupting drug trafficking networks, identifying sophisticated concealment methods and preventing illicit substances from reaching communities across the country.
